Geographic map projections, great-circle arcs, and spatial network plotting

plot_graph_map.Rd

R-native equivalent of graph-tool's Basemap/Cartopy geographic plotting integration. Runs 100% offline with zero external GIS or Python dependencies using pure-R cartographic projections, spherical great-circle interpolation, and built-in low-resolution world coastlines (with support for custom user-supplied polygon data frames).

Usage

project_coords(lon, lat,
  projection = c("robinson", "mercator", "equirectangular", "mollweide",
  "orthographic"), lon0 = 0, lat0 = 0)

great_circle_arc(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2, n = 24L)

world_coastlines()

plot_graph_map(graph, lon, lat,
  projection = c("robinson", "mercator", "equirectangular", "mollweide",
  "orthographic"), lon0 = 0, lat0 = 0, xlim = NULL, ylim = NULL,
  geodesic = TRUE, n_arc = 24L, coastlines = TRUE, polygons = NULL,
  graticule = TRUE, land_col = "#ECEAE4", border_col = "#94A3B8",
  ocean_col = "#E0F2FE",
  graticule_col = grDevices::adjustcolor("#64748B", 0.30),
  vertex_color = "#D62828", vertex_border = "#1F2937", vertex_size = 1.2,
  vertex_label = NULL, vertex_label_cex = 0.7, vertex_label_pos = 3L,
  edge_color = grDevices::adjustcolor("#1D4ED8", 0.55), edge_lwd = 1.1,
  eorder = NULL, vorder = NULL, arrows = NULL, arrow_length = 0.06,
  main = NULL, output = NULL, width = 9, height = 5, dpi = 150, ...)

Arguments

lon, lat

Numeric vectors of longitudes (degrees East) and latitudes (degrees North).

projection

Cartographic map projection: "robinson", "mercator", "equirectangular", "mollweide", or "orthographic".

lon0, lat0

Central meridian and central parallel (degrees) for the projection.

lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2

Start and end geographic coordinates (degrees) for great_circle_arc().

n

Number of interpolation points along the spherical great-circle arc.

graph

A graph created by graph_create.

xlim, ylim

Optional geographic bounding box (c(lon_min, lon_max) and c(lat_min, lat_max)) for regional maps.

geodesic

Logical; if TRUE, draw edges along spherical great-circle routes split cleanly across the antimeridian.

n_arc

Number of points per geodesic edge arc.

coastlines

Logical; whether to draw coastline land polygons.

polygons

Optional custom data frame with columns lon, lat, and optional group (defaults to built-in offline world_coastlines()).

graticule

Logical; whether to draw latitude/longitude grid lines.

land_col, border_col, ocean_col, graticule_col

Basemap colours.

vertex_color, vertex_border, vertex_size, vertex_label, vertex_label_cex, vertex_label_pos

Vertex aesthetics and label placement.

edge_color, edge_lwd, eorder, vorder, arrows, arrow_length

Edge aesthetics, z-ordering, and arrowheads.

main

Optional title.

output

Optional destination file path exported via save_graph_plot (PDF, SVG, EPS, PNG, JPEG, TIFF).

width, height, dpi

Output dimensions (inches) and raster DPI when output is supplied.

...

Additional arguments forwarded to points.

Value

project_coords() returns a data frame with columns x, y, and visible. great_circle_arc() returns a data frame with columns lon, lat, and segment. world_coastlines() returns a data frame with columns lon, lat, group, and region. plot_graph_map() invisibly returns a list containing projected, projection, lon0, and lat0.

Examples

g <- graph_create(4L, directed = FALSE)
graph_add_edges(g, rbind(c(1L, 2L), c(2L, 3L), c(3L, 4L), c(4L, 1L)))
lon <- c(-74.0, -0.1, 139.7, -118.2)
lat <- c(40.7, 51.5, 35.7, 34.0)
plot_graph_map(g, lon = lon, lat = lat, projection = "robinson",
               vertex_label = c("NYC", "LON", "TYO", "LAX"),
               output = tempfile(fileext = ".pdf"))
